description: Generated from core/internal/settings. Values live under `settings:` in the config file; change them with `procauto settings set <key> <value>`.

^routines\\.[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*\\.builtin.description: Agent CLI built-in tools the run may use, allowed explicitly, in the backend's own names: claude-code's tools (e.g. Read, Grep, Bash, Edit); on codex shell, write (the sandbox may write in the run's folder), network (with write), web_search, view_image. Dry runs get only those that can't change anything. Defaults to `automator.builtinTools` in the routine's file.

^routines\\.[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*\\.concurr.description: queue waits for other queued runs (one at a time on this device, tightest staleness first); parallel runs alongside them. A routine never overlaps itself either way. Defaults to `automator.concurrency` in the routine's file.

^routines\\.[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*\\.effort$.description: How hard the model thinks; default leaves it to the model backend. Defaults to `automator.effort` in the routine's file.

^routines\\.[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*\\.enabled.description: Whether the routine runs on its schedule. Defaults to `automator.enabled` in the routine's file.

^routines\\.[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*\\.folder$.description: Folder the run works in (agent CLI backends), with its project instructions added to the routine's (CLAUDE.md on claude-code, AGENTS.md on codex). Without one, runs work in an empty temporary folder, or, with session save, in an empty folder of the routine's own that's kept. Defaults to `automator.folder` in the routine's file.

^routines\\.[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*\\.params\.description: A routine parameter's value (declared in its file's automator.parameters, with its type and default; required ones have no default).

^routines\\.[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*\\.schedul.description: When the routine runs (cron, local time). A routine without one runs only by hand. Defaults to `automator.schedule` in the routine's file.

^routines\\.[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*\\.session.description: save keeps the agent CLI session and records its ID, folder and backend with the run, so it can be resumed from that folder with that backend's CLI (the routine's folder, or one of its own when it has none); discard leaves nothing behind. Defaults to `automator.session` in the routine's file.

^routines\\.[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*\\.stalene.description: How late a missed run may still run before it's recorded as missed. Defaults to `automator.staleness` in the routine's file.

^routines\\.[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*\\.timeout.description: How long a run may take before it's stopped and recorded as failed. Defaults to `automator.timeout` in the routine's file.

history.retention-days.description: How long run history and logs are kept.

llm.budget.weekly-usd.description: API spend allowed in the rolling 7 days (0: no limit); past it, scheduled runs don't start.

llm.budget.window.description: Length of the rolling short budget window.

llm.budget.window-usd.description: API spend allowed in the rolling short window (0: no limit); past it, scheduled runs don't start.

llm.local.keep-alive.description: How long the local server keeps the model loaded after the last request from anyone, sent with each request (Ollama's keep_alive; other servers ignore it). 0 unloads after each request; empty leaves the server's own.

llm.local.model.description: The model the local backend runs routines on: its name on the server (e.g. qwen3:8b; `ollama list` shows the ones pulled). It replaces the model a routine names, unless that's local/<model>, another model on the same server.

llm.local.url.description: Experimental, untested: the OpenAI-compatible server the local backend runs routines on, and claude-api runs routines whose model is local/<model> on. The default is Ollama on this machine; llama.cpp's llama-server, vLLM, LM Studio and hosted APIs such as DeepSeek, Qwen (DashScope) or Kimi (Moonshot) work too. A server that needs an API key gets it with `auth login local`. Its runs have no list price, so they don't count toward the llm.budget.* budgets.

llm.usage-limit.description: Scheduled runs don't start while the Claude plan's 5-hour or weekly usage is above this share (they're recorded as skipped); runs started by hand still run. A run that hits the plan's limit stops scheduled runs until it resets.

memories.max-chars.description: How much each memories file may hold (every routine's, and each routine's own): what a run's prompt gets, kept small. Past it, `memory add` asks to compact first.

plugins.open-apps.description: Keep open the apps plugins need (iMCP, say): the scheduler opens one in the background when it isn't running and a routine or hook that's on uses its plugin. Off, setup says when one isn't running; a run still opens it before connecting to its plugin.

runs.failure-notifications.description: Notify me when a run fails, needs a sign-in, or is skipped or missed (clicking one opens the app on the run).

update.auto.description: Install new releases by themselves, at a quiet moment: once a release has been out an hour, when nothing is running or about to, the app's window isn't open and the computer has been awake a while. A notification says when one is installed, or failed.

update.source-dir.description: Source checkout `update` builds from when no published release has a download for this machine. Empty: the checkout this build came from.
